text:
maria: heads-up — seeing a puzzling split after int8 bring-up on rerank-v3.

maria: p@1 improved vs fp32 (+2.1%) but ndcg@10 dropped (-3.4%) on short-query holdout.

jake: can you paste the numbers and run-id?

maria: run-id: run/2026-03-21-42
maria: holdout: short-query cohort (3,120 queries)
maria: p@1: +2.1% (0.612 -> 0.625)
maria: ndcg@10: -3.4% (0.442 -> 0.427)
maria: ndcg_short_query: -7.9% (0.482 -> 0.444)

sana: interesting — maybe tie-breaking or candidate-ordering changed; quant noise can move the top item up for many queries but hurt deeper rank.

lee: steps I'd try:
- rerun with deterministic seed
- preserve candidate order in eval
- compare softmax rescale / score calibration

lee: quick command:
```bash
eval-harness run \
  --model rerank-v3-int8 \
  --holdout short-query \
  --seed 42 \
  --preserve-order \
  --rescale softmax \
  --out /tmp/rerank_int8_short.json
```

jake: also add precision@5 and MRR, and per-query tie-counts. p@1 up doesn't rule out ndcg loss.

maria: good call. I'll add precision@5, mrr, p@k curve to the dashboard and upload a diff of per-query deltas.

sana: also check tokenizer parity between the fp32 and int8 docker images — subtle whitespace/casing changes have bitten us before.

maria: agreed. plan:
1) lee runs deterministic preserve-order eval
2) jake expands metrics and dashboard
3) maria diffs per-query ranking deltas and sanity-check tokenizer
4) if reproduces, test softmax rescale and doc-normalization

lee: assigned, running now. ETA ~2h.

eval-bot: scheduled job run/2026-03-21-42 started (id: 9876), posting results when complete :robot_face:

maria: thanks — please ping here when the run lands. if it's a false alarm we close, otherwise open an eval-ticket with sample queries attached.

jake: will add ticket template and metric thresholds (ndcg drop >2% or ndcg_short_query drop >5%)

maria: done — ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/ML-7854

lee: run finished. preliminary: p@1 +1.9%, ndcg@10 -3.5%, per-query diff attached (uploaded to /artifacts/runs/9876/deltas.csv)

maria: thanks. I'll start digging into top-k tie shifts and tokenization parity.

sana: if we confirm it's quant noise, we can try hybrid-quant or recalibration (temperature) to recover ndcg without losing p@1.

maria: noted. closing loop later.
